proof_summary: For the graph on primes \(\{2,3,5,7,11,13,19\}\), joining differently ending pairs with product at most \(150\), every vertex cover has product at least \(2\cdot3\cdot5\cdot7\cdot11=2310\); hence any \(d\le2025\) misses both endpoints \(p,q\) of some edge. Since \(d\) is then invertible modulo \(pq\), some \(i<pq\le150\) makes \(pq\mid a+id\), giving that term two prime divisors with different final digits.
